item.title: Tropical Storm Edouard Public Advisory Number 5a
item.description:
Issued at 100 PM CDT Tue Sep 01 2026 
000
WTNT35 KNHC 011748
TCPAT5
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Edouard Intermediate Advisory Number 5A
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL052026
100 PM CDT Tue Sep 01 2026

...EDOUARD EXPECTED TO MAKE LANDFALL ALONG THE NORTHWESTERN GULF 
COAST SHORTLY...
...TROPICAL STORM CONDITIONS SPREADING ACROSS THE WARNING AREA...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 100 PM CDT...1800 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...29.7N 93.6W
ABOUT 20 MI...30 KM WSW OF CAMERON LOUISIANA
ABOUT 25 MI...35 KM SE OF PORT ARTHUR TEXAS
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...50 MPH...85 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 305 DEGREES AT 8 MPH...13 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1000 MB...29.53 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
The Hurricane Watch has been discontinued.

The Storm Surge Warning has been discontinued. A Coastal Flood 
Warning has been issued by the National Weather Service for portions 
of the northwestern Gulf Coast.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* Port Bolivar, Texas to the Vermilion/Iberia Parish Line
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area.
 
For storm information specific to your area, including possible
inland watches and warnings, please monitor products issued by your
local National Weather Service forecast office.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 100 PM CDT (1800 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Edouard was
located near latitude 29.7 North, longitude 93.6 West. Edouard is
moving toward the northwest near 8 mph (13 km/h), and this motion is
expected to continue through early Wednesday. On the forecast 
track, the center of Edouard is forecast to reach the northwestern 
Gulf Coast within the warning area later today and move inland over 
southeast Texas tonight.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 50 mph (85 km/h) with higher gusts. 
Little change in strength is expected before Edouard makes landfall 
shortly. Rapid weakening is expected after the center moves inland.
 
Edouard is a small tropical cyclone. Tropical-storm-force winds 
extend outward up to 25 miles (35 km) from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1000 mb (29.53 inches). A 
National Ocean Service station at Calcasieu Pass, Louisiana, 
recently reported a sustained wind of 44 mph (71 km/h) and a gust 
of 52 mph (84 km/h).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Tropical Storm Edouard can be found in the
Tropical Cyclone Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDAT5 and WMO
header WTNT45 KNHC.
 
WIND: Tropical storm conditions are spreading across portions of 
the warning area along the northwestern Gulf Coast.
 
STORM SURGE: The combination of storm surge and tide will cause
normally dry areas near the coast to be flooded by rising waters
moving inland from the shoreline. The water could reach the
following heights above ground somewhere in the indicated areas if
the peak surge occurs at the time of high tide...
 
High Island, TX to Vermilion/Cameron Parish Line, LA...1-3 ft
 
The deepest water will occur along the immediate coast near and to
the right of the center. Surge-related flooding depends on the
relative timing of the surge and the tidal cycle, and can vary
greatly over short distances. For information specific to your
area, please see products issued by your local National Weather
Service forecast office.
 
For a complete depiction of areas at risk of storm surge inundation,
please see the National Weather Service Peak Storm Surge Graphic,
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_at5.shtml?peakSurge.
 
RAINFALL: Edouard is expected to produce rainfall totals of 3 to 6
inches with maximum totals up to 9 inches for parts of the Upper
Texas Coast inland through east-central Texas, with potential for 2
to 4 inches in far southwest Louisiana. This rainfall is likely to
produce flash flooding, especially in low-lying and urban areas.
River flooding may also be possible.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with
Edouard, please see the National Weather Service Storm Total
Rainfall Graphic available at
hurricanes.gov/graphics_at5.shtml?rainqpf and the Flash Flood Risk
graphic at hurricanes.gov/graphics_at5.shtml?ero.
 
TORNADOES: A tornado or two is possible this afternoon and evening
over parts of southwest Louisiana and southeast Texas.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 400 PM CDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Reinhart

item.title: Tropical Storm Edouard Forecast Discussion Number 5
item.description:
Issued at 1000 AM CDT Tue Sep 01 2026 
000
WTNT45 KNHC 011446
TCDAT5
 
Tropical Storm Edouard Discussion Number   5
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL052026
1000 AM CDT Tue Sep 01 2026
 
Edouard is a small but strengthening tropical storm. The center has 
been trackable this morning using NWS radar data from Lake Charles, 
Louisiana (KLCH), and recent data show the inner-core structure of 
the system is becoming better organized. There has been a notable 
increase in deep convection near and to the south of the center, and 
a recent dropsonde released in that area reported mean boundary 
layer winds of 61 kt. Doppler velocities have also notably 
strengthened during the past couple of hours, and adjusting these 
data to estimate a surface wind support raising the initial 
intensity to 45 kt. The last center dropsonde from the Air Force 
Hurricane Hunters showed the central pressure has fallen to 1000 mb.
 
Environmental and oceanic conditions are conducive for additional 
strengthening for as long as the center remains offshore. With very 
warm Gulf waters and weak vertical wind shear, the hurricane 
regional models continue to highlight the potential for continued 
strengthening through landfall. The 12-h forecast point for Edouard 
is well inland, but note that additional strengthening is expected 
that cannot be easily reflected in the official forecast. A Tropical 
Storm Warning and Hurricane Watch remain in effect for portions of 
the Upper Texas coast and southwestern Louisiana. Given the improved 
radar structure of Edouard and the expectation of additional 
strengthening, NHC will issue hourly Tropical Cyclone Updates (TCU) 
beginning at 1100 am CDT (16 UTC). Once inland, Edouard is likely 
to rapidly weaken and should dissipate on Wednesday.

Some short-term wobbles have been observed in radar data during the 
past few hours, but the longer-term motion of Edouard is 
northwestward (305/7 kt). This general motion is expected to 
continue through tonight, which will bring the center of Edouard 
onshore near the Texas/Louisiana border within the warning area this 
afternoon and then inland across southeastern Texas tonight. The 
updated NHC track forecast lies slightly to the right of the 
previous prediction based on the latest consensus trends.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Edouard is strengthening as it approaches the northwest Gulf 
Coast, and tropical storm conditions are beginning along the 
southwestern Louisiana and Upper Texas coasts. Hurricane conditions, 
especially in gusts, are still possible from High Island to Cameron 
later today.
 
2. A Storm Surge Warning is in effect along the immediate coast from 
High Island, Texas, to the Vermilion/Cameron Parish Line, Louisiana, 
where peak values of 3 to 5 feet above ground level are possible.
 
3. Heavy rain will impact parts of the Upper Texas coast through 
east-central Texas into far Southwest Louisiana today and Wednesday 
as Edouard tracks inland. Flash flooding is likely across this 
region, especially in urban areas. River flooding may also be 
possible.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  01/1500Z 29.4N  93.3W   45 KT  50 MPH
 12H  02/0000Z 30.2N  94.2W   40 KT  45 MPH...INLAND
 24H  02/1200Z 31.2N  95.2W   25 KT  30 MPH...POST-TROP/INLAND
 36H  03/0000Z...DISSIPATED
 
$$
Forecaster Reinhart

item.title: Tropical Storm Edouard Public Advisory Update Number
item.description:
Issued at 1200 PM CDT Tue Sep 01 2026 
000
WTNT65 KNHC 011657
TCUAT5
 
Tropical Storm Edouard Tropical Cyclone Update
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL052026
1200 PM CDT Tue Sep 01 2026
 
...TROPICAL STORM CONDITIONS SPREADING ACROSS THE SOUTHWESTERN 
LOUISIANA AND UPPER TEXAS COASTS...
...1200 PM CDT POSITION UPDATE...

WSR-88D radar data from Lake Charles, Louisiana, and Houston, Texas, 
indicate that Edouard's maximum sustained winds remain near 50 mph 
(85 km/h).

A National Ocean Service station near Calcasieu Pass, Louisiana, 
(CAPL1) recently reported a wind gust to 51 mph (81 km/h). A 
WeatherFlow station near Cameron, Louisiana, recently reported a 
wind gust to 46 mph (74 km/h). A National Ocean Service station near 
Texas Point, Texas, (TXPT2) recently reported a wind gust to 39 mph 
(63 km/h).
 
SUMMARY OF 1200 PM CDT...1700 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...29.6N 93.5W
ABOUT 20 MI...30 KM SW OF CAMERON LOUISIANA
ABOUT 30 MI...50 KM SE OF PORT ARTHUR TEXAS
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...50 MPH...85 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 305 DEGREES AT 8 MPH...13 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1000 MB...29.53 INCHES
 
$$
